note: The construction table of PREREG-SEC27. sec27-brief-counts.mjs checks every frozen item against its row; sec27-tellsim.mjs --table checks the table for cross-item ROLE tells and sec27-semcheck.mjs --table for SEMANTIC templates. Each author owns whole rule families (the family column) so concurrent authors cannot converge. Edit only by an amendment written before the probe, and re-run both checks.

slots.frame: Two independent clauses; the second opens with a determiner + noun phrase that reads as an appositive of the first clause's last noun until its verb arrives 6+ words later. The second clause reports a LATER, separate event, so it neither explains nor restates the first
slots.lures: the comma (appositive reading); the colon (a reader who takes the second clause as an explanation); no mark (run-on)
slots.decided: the second clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4. The colon must die on the RELATION (the second clause is a later event, not an explanation), never on a second colon elsewhere in the sentence (SEC26: two authors converged on 'one colon per sentence')

slots.frame: A singular head whose number has to be found past a modifier; 'is V-en' against 'was V-en'; a present 'unless' or 'provided that' clause 5+ words after the blank fixes the present
slots.misleader: a plural noun in the subject; 'was V-en' pulls because the passage narrates a past study
slots.lever: H4: the conditional is the only tense evidence; no time word anywhere in the blank's sentence
slots.decider: a present-tense 'unless' / 'provided that' clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: An opening 'Whereas/Although the [PLURAL NP] rarely ___,' whose elided verb is the main clause's lexical PRESENT verb (not 'have' + participle); the main clause's subject is singular
slots.misleader: the singular main-clause subject after the blank pulls 'does'; 'have' pulls because the main verb sounds like a completed result
slots.lever: H1, H4 (cataphoric ellipsis has been panel-hard in every batch since v22: SEC22B-05, SEC23B-06, SEC24A-06, SEC24B-01, SEC25B-05, SEC26B-05)
slots.decider: the main clause's lexical present verb, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Two sentences: the second opens with a long noun phrase that reads as an appositive of the first sentence's last noun until its verb arrives 6+ words later; it makes a separate claim (a contrast or a new finding), not an explanation
slots.lures: the comma (appositive reading); the colon (explanation reading); no mark
slots.decided: the second sentence's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4. As A1: the colon dies on the relation (a contrast or new claim is not an explanation)

slots.frame: Perfect progressive KEYED by a DURATION phrase ('for nine seasons', 'for three winters'), 5+ words after the blank, running up to the present; the lure is the PRESENT progressive ('are V-ing'), not a past form. No 'since' anywhere
slots.misleader: 'are V-ing' pulls as the plain description of an ongoing activity; a singular noun near the blank pulls the verb
slots.lever: H4; the perfect is decided without 'since' (SEC26: 'since' keyed the perfect 4/4 and both readers named it)
slots.decider: a duration phrase ('for N [units]'), 5+ words after the blank, inside the blank's sentence

slots.frame: Possessive pronoun, MATCHED (plural verb + 'their'), the plural owner named in the PREVIOUS sentence; a singular noun in the blank's sentence gives 'its' a believable but grammatically excluded owner (it is inside a phrase that cannot own the object)
slots.misleader: the singular noun pulls 'its'; the matched key looks like 'copy the subject'
slots.lever: H2 (matched numbers on different nouns); antecedent one sentence back
slots.decider: the previous sentence's plural owner

slots.frame: A plural subject whose number must be KNOWN (a plural that reads singular, or a compound joined by 'and' whose second member is long); 'are V-ing' against 'were V-ing'; a present 'as long as' or 'provided that' clause 5+ words after
slots.misleader: the subject reads singular; 'were V-ing' pulls because the passage reports past fieldwork
slots.lever: H3, H4
slots.decider: a present-tense conditional clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: A verb of reporting or finding (showed, suggested, confirmed) whose object is a content clause with 'that' omitted; the clause's subject is a long noun phrase whose verb arrives 6+ words later, so it can be read as the start of a new sentence. No mark is correct
slots.lures: the semicolon and the dash (new-clause reading); the comma (the reader pauses after the reporting verb)
slots.decided: the content clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; the delayed-verb family keys a semicolon (A1), a period (A4) and NO MARK here

slots.frame: An opening 'Although the [SINGULAR NP] usually ___,' whose elided predicate is the main clause's be + ADJECTIVE (so be, not do); the main clause's subject is plural
slots.misleader: the plural main-clause subject after the blank pulls 'are'; 'does' pulls because 'usually' reads as a habitual action
slots.lever: H1, H4 (be-ellipsis: the elided predicate is an adjective, 5+ words after the blank)
slots.decider: the main clause's predicate adjective, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: SINGULAR POSSESSIVE. A fact INSIDE the blank's sentence implies exactly one owner (a title, a role, a superlative: 'the colony's founding queen', 'the ward's chief surgeon'), with no count word anywhere in the passage; the noun after the blank can be read as a verb
slots.lures: the plural possessive; the plain plural (garden path)
slots.decided: a fact inside the blank's sentence that implies one owner (no count word)
slots.lever: H7 by inference, not a count (SEC26: the four noun items were all decided by a count in another sentence and graders grouped them)

slots.frame: Sentence-final RESTRICTIVE participial phrase; a LATER sentence contrasts another set of the noun ('The cores drilled in winter, by contrast, ...'), so the phrase is needed to say which. No count word anywhere in the passage
slots.lures: the comma and the dash (nonrestrictive reading); the period (a reader who takes the phrase as a new sentence)
slots.decided: a contrast in a LATER sentence (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)
slots.lever: H7; the contrast is in a later sentence, never a count in the sentence before (SEC26: 'the deciding count sits in the preceding sentence', 7 items)

slots.frame: 'were V-en' against 'are V-en'; the past is INFERRED, not announced: a phrase naming a finished era or a superseded instrument ('before the first satellites', 'in the age of hand-cranked seismographs', 'under the old survey datum') 5+ words after; no year, no 'ago', no 'last', no when/while clause with a past verb
slots.misleader: 'are V-en' reads as a general statement about the instrument; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4: the time frame needs inference (SEC26: 'a closed past phrase always means simple past', readers' named rule)
slots.decider: a phrase naming a finished era or superseded practice, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Passive present perfect KEYED by a PRESENT-RESULT clause in the same sentence ('..., so the gauge now reads...' is banned: no 'now/still/already'; write '..., and the replacement gauge reads two degrees higher'), with NO since, NO duration phrase and NO time word in the blank's sentence. 'was V-en' must be wrong because the result clause is present and nothing places the action in a closed past
slots.misleader: 'was V-en' pulls because the action sounds finished; a plural noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4; the perfect is decided without 'since' or a duration
slots.decider: a present-tense clause in the blank's sentence stating the current result

slots.frame: The blank is the auxiliary + shared 'always'; a 3+ word adverbial and then the past participle of a verb that cannot be passive or adjectival here (an intransitive: 'drifted', 'subsided', 'erupted') settles have over be; a singular head
slots.misleader: 'is always' reads as the plain present; a plural noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4 (SEC25A-07's mechanism with a new shared adverb and a new option set)
slots.decider: the intransitive participle, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Sentence-final NONRESTRICTIVE participial phrase; a fact INSIDE the blank's sentence makes the noun unique (a superlative, a proper name, a possessive with one possible referent: 'the observatory's largest mirror'), so the phrase adds information. No count word anywhere in the passage; no dash offered
slots.lures: no mark (restrictive reading); the period (fragment); the colon (a participial phrase that modifies the noun is not an explanation of the clause)
slots.decided: a fact inside the blank's sentence that makes the noun unique (inference, no count word)
slots.lever: H7 by inference

slots.frame: By-agent pronoun, present passive, MISMATCHED (singular verb + 'by them'); the plural agent is named TWO sentences back (the passage's first sentence); the noun just before the blank is singular and is the believable referent for 'it'
slots.misleader: the singular noun before the blank pulls 'it'; the plural agent pulls 'are'
slots.lever: H2; the antecedent is far (two sentences back)
slots.decider: the plural agent named two sentences back

slots.frame: 'was being V-en' against 'is being V-en'; the past is INFERRED from a phrase naming a finished state of the world ('while the old causeway still carried traffic' is banned: 'still' and 'while + past'; write 'in the final months of the steam era', 'during the survey's first, unmapped decade'); no year, no ago
slots.misleader: 'is being V-en' reads as the default description of work in progress; a plural noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4 (the batch's only 'being' grid)
slots.decider: a phrase naming a finished era, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Active present perfect KEYED against the past progressive by a PRESENT-RESULT clause ('..., and the channel is now dry' is banned for 'now'; write '..., which is why the channel carries no water'), with no since, no duration and no time word in the blank's sentence
slots.misleader: 'were V-ing' pulls because the activity sounds like background narration; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4; the second present-result row; its result clause must differ in shape from B3's (a 'which is why' clause, a 'so' clause, a coordinated present clause)
slots.decider: a present-tense clause in the blank's sentence stating the current result

slots.frame: The blank is the auxiliary + shared 'also'; a 3+ word adverbial and then a predicate ADJECTIVE ('unstable', 'inaccessible') settles be over have ('have also ... unstable' needs 'been'); a plural head
slots.misleader: 'have also' pulls as the default with an adverb; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4
slots.decider: the predicate adjective, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Sentence-final NONRESTRICTIVE appositive set off by a dash; the passage's FIRST sentence (two sentences before the blank's) establishes there is only one of the noun, IN A WORD THAT NEEDS READING (a role or a title, e.g. 'the station's sole seismometer' is banned as a count word; write 'the station's seismometer, installed when the station opened,'), never in the sentence just before; no comma offered
slots.lures: no mark (restrictive reading); the period (fragment); the comma one word off
slots.decided: a fact two sentences before the blank's sentence (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence; never the sentence just before)
slots.lever: H7

slots.frame: Garden path after an opening subordinate clause: the noun phrase after the clause's verb could be its object or the main clause's subject; the main verb 6+ words later shows it is the SUBJECT, so the comma goes BEFORE it (the early position)
slots.lures: the comma after the noun phrase (object reading); no comma; the colon after the subordinate clause
slots.decided: the main clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; C9 keys the late position

slots.frame: 'is + shared word' against 'was + shared word'; a habitual 'whenever' clause with a present verb, 5+ words after the blank; a singular subject after an opening phrase whose noun is plural
slots.misleader: the opening plural; 'was' pulls because the passage reports an archive's history
slots.lever: H4 (the batch's one habitual cue; explicit by design, counted in SC4)
slots.decider: a 'whenever' clause with a present verb, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Passive present perfect KEYED by 'since' + a past-tense clause, 5+ words after the blank; the lure is the PRESENT passive ('are V-en'), not a past form, so 'since' does not simply mean 'not the past'
slots.misleader: 'are V-en' pulls as the plain description; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4; the batch's ONE since-decided perfect (SEC26 had four, keyed 4/4)
slots.decider: 'since' + a past-tense clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: A complete clause, then 'then' (or 'later', 'afterward') + a NOUN PHRASE with no verb ('...recorded one tremor, then a second, weaker one near the coast'); a reader who expects a clause after 'then' reaches for the semicolon. No verb ever arrives
slots.lures: the semicolon (new-clause reading); no mark; the colon
slots.decided: no finite verb arrives after 'then' (quote the noun phrase's last word, 6+ words after the blank)
slots.lever: H4; graders must find that no verb comes

slots.frame: Object pronoun, MISMATCHED (plural verb + 'it'); the singular antecedent sits in the SAME clause, just before the blank, as the object of a preposition inside the subject (so the nearest noun IS the antecedent); a plural noun elsewhere in the sentence gives 'them' a believable referent
slots.misleader: the singular noun just before the blank pulls the verb to singular; the plural noun pulls 'them'
slots.lever: H2; here the nearest noun is the antecedent (SEC26: the wrong pronoun was always the nearest noun)
slots.decider: the singular noun in the same clause

slots.frame: 'was V-ing' against 'is V-ing'; a 'when' clause with a past verb 5+ words after (an interrupted action); a singular head whose number must be found past a long modifier ending on a plural noun
slots.misleader: the plural noun at the end of the modifier; 'is V-ing' as the default description
slots.lever: H3, H4 (the batch's one explicit past clause; counted in SC3 and SC4)
slots.decider: a past 'when' clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: 'were V-en' KEYED against 'have been V-en' (the participle 9+ letters, for the length ratio). 'since' appears ONCE, in a relative or opening clause that belongs to ANOTHER verb ('The chapels, which have stood empty since the parishes merged, ___ crowded during ...'); the blank's own verb is fixed in a closed past by a phrase naming one finished event, 5+ words after
slots.misleader: 'since' in the sentence pulls 'have been V-en' (the SEC26 rule 'since means perfect'); a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4; breaks 'since means perfect' on purpose
slots.decider: a phrase naming one finished event, 5+ words after the blank (NOT the since clause)

slots.frame: The blank is 'seldom' + the auxiliary ({seldom is, seldom are, seldom does, seldom do}); a 3+ word adverbial and then an -ING form ('copying', 'touring') settles be over do ('do ... copying' is ungrammatical; 'do ... copy' would need the bare verb); a plural head
slots.misleader: 'seldom do' pulls as the idiomatic order with 'seldom'; a singular noun near the blank pulls 'is'
slots.lever: H4
slots.decider: the -ing form, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Garden path after an opening subordinate clause: the noun phrase after the clause's verb IS its object; the main clause's own subject arrives after it, and its verb 6+ words later, so the comma goes AFTER the noun phrase (the late position: the keyed option ends in its comma)
slots.lures: the comma before the noun phrase (subject reading); no comma; a semicolon at the early position
slots.decided: the main clause's subject and verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; the trailing-comma shape is KEYED here (SEC26: 'trailing-comma options always lose', 4/5)

slots.frame: PLAIN PLURAL keyed. The word after the blank is a VERB that can also be read as a noun, and the plural is fixed by a fact in the blank's OWN sentence (an 'and'-joined pair of owners, or a plural verb later in the clause), never by a count in another sentence
slots.lures: the plural possessive (the next word read as a noun); the singular possessive
slots.decided: the verb after the blank, plus the blank's own sentence
slots.lever: H7 without a count elsewhere

slots.frame: A COMPLETE clause whose last words could still be taking an object ('The survey isolated two factors', '...measured only what it could count'), then a sentence-final list or appositive that explains it; the reader must decide whether the clause before the blank is complete. No dash offered
slots.lures: the comma (a series that starts too early); no mark (the list read as the verb's object); the semicolon (no clause follows)
slots.decided: whether the clause before the blank is complete, and what follows explains it
slots.lever: H4; a colon key where the colon is not the lone strong mark

slots.frame: 'are + shared word' against 'were + shared word'; the present is INFERRED from a present-tense clause in the same sentence describing a current state ('..., a gap the agency's handbook describes in its opening chapter'), with no time word (no now, currently, today)
slots.misleader: 'were' pulls because the passage reports a past survey; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4: the present must be inferred
slots.decider: a present-tense clause in the blank's sentence describing a current state

slots.frame: 'were V-ing' KEYED against 'have been V-ing'; the closed past is INFERRED from a phrase naming a finished institution or period ('in the years of the old ration-book system', 'under the abolished poll tax'), 5+ words after; no year, no ago, no when + past verb
slots.misleader: 'have been V-ing' pulls because the activity sounds ongoing; a singular noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4
slots.decider: a phrase naming a finished period, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Anaphoric ellipsis at the end of a sentence: '..., and the [PLURAL NP] ___ too' (shared 'too'), where the elided predicate is an earlier have + participle ('had/has risen', so 'have', not 'are'); the earlier clause's subject is singular
slots.misleader: the earlier singular subject pulls 'has'; 'are' pulls because the antecedent clause reads as a state
slots.lever: H1, H4: the elided participle is 5+ words before the blank, in another clause
slots.decider: the earlier clause's participle, 5+ words before the blank

slots.frame: A verb (or a verb + particle: 'set out', 'laid out', 'ruled out') whose DELAYED OBJECT is a long noun phrase that reads as a new clause or an appositive; no verb follows, because the noun phrase is the object. No mark is correct
slots.lures: the comma and the dash (appositive reading); the semicolon (new-clause reading)
slots.decided: the verb's need for an object: the long noun phrase after the blank is its object
slots.lever: H4 (the mechanism of 'no mark before a delayed object', with a particle verb and a new frame)

slots.frame: Object pronoun, MATCHED (singular verb + 'it'); the singular antecedent is in an OPENING clause of the same sentence; the noun just before the blank is plural and gives 'them' a believable but excluded referent
slots.misleader: the plural noun before the blank pulls 'were' and 'them'
slots.lever: H2: matched numbers on different nouns
slots.decider: the opening clause's singular noun

slots.frame: 'was + shared word' KEYED against 'has been + shared word'; an explicit closed-past phrase ('in the spring of that year', 'during the 1990s census' is banned for the year: write 'during that census') 5+ words after; no since anywhere
slots.misleader: 'has been' pulls because the state sounds lasting; a plural noun near the blank
slots.lever: H4 (the batch's one explicit closed-past phrase; counted in SC3 and SC4)
slots.decider: an explicit closed-past phrase, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Anaphoric ellipsis in a comparison or contrast: '..., as the [SINGULAR NP] often ___' (shared 'often'), the elided verb a PRESENT lexical verb earlier in the sentence; 'was' pulls because a nearby clause is past
slots.misleader: a plural noun before the blank pulls 'do'; 'was' pulls because a nearby clause narrates the past
slots.lever: H1, H4
slots.decider: the earlier lexical present verb, 5+ words before the blank

slots.frame: A complete clause, then a sentence-final noun phrase that EXPLAINS it ('One variable mattered more than the rest ___ the distance between home and the nearest clinic'); the noun phrase reads as the start of a clause until no verb arrives. No comma and no dash offered (either could be defensible)
slots.lures: the semicolon (second-clause reading); no mark; the comma one word off
slots.decided: no finite verb ever arrives (quote the modifier word where a clause would need its verb, 6+ words after the blank)
slots.lever: H4 (SEC26D-09 was non-exclusive 3/3 because a comma was keyed with a colon offered; here the colon is keyed and no comma is offered)

slots.frame: PLURAL POSSESSIVE. A LATER sentence (never the sentence before) shows several owners by what they DO ('Each of the councils then ...' is banned; write 'The councils later disagreed about ...'); the noun after the blank can be read as a verb
slots.lures: the plain plural (garden path); the singular possessive
slots.decided: a fact in a LATER sentence (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)
slots.lever: H7
